title: Fewest Repaints for a Dark Stretch
statement:
You get a string blocks made of the letters 'W' (a white tile) and 'B' (a black tile), and an integer k. In one move you may repaint a single white tile black.

Return the fewest moves needed so that somewhere in the row there are at least k black tiles in a row.

examples.why: Repaint index 2: "WBBBBBW" now has five black tiles in a row. No 4-wide stretch is already all black.
The first two tiles are already black.
Growing the longest black run "BBB" to 6 tiles costs 3. The last six tiles "BBWBWB" have only two white tiles. The best stretch need not contain the longest run.

hints: For a fixed stretch of k tiles, how many moves does it take to make it all black?
Exactly the number of white tiles in it. So you want the k-wide window with the fewest whites.
Count the whites in the first window, then slide: add 1 if the tile entering is white, subtract 1 if the tile leaving is white, and keep the minimum.

explain.intuition:
Whatever stretch of k tiles you end up making black, it costs exactly the number of white tiles inside it, and repainting tiles outside it never helps. So the question is just: which window of length k has the fewest 'W's?

Counting each window from scratch is O(n · k). Sliding the window by one tile only changes two tiles: one enters on the right, one leaves on the left. Adjust the count by those two and you get every window in O(n), the same way a scroll handler can update a "visible items" total from just the rows that entered and left the viewport.
steps: Count the white tiles in blocks[0..k−1]; that is whites and also the current best.
For i from k to n − 1: if blocks[i] is white, add 1; if blocks[i − k] is white, subtract 1.
pitfalls: Extending the longest existing black run. The cheapest window can be elsewhere, as in the third example.
Forgetting the last window, for example by looping i < n − 1. In "WWWBB" with k = 2 the answer 0 is only in the last window.
Counting black tiles and returning k − maxBlack is correct, but returning maxBlack or mixing up the two counts is a common slip.

solutions.title: Count every window
solutions.idea: For each start position, count the white tiles in the next k tiles.

solutions.title: Fixed-size sliding window
solutions.idea: Keep the white count of the current window and adjust it by the tile entering and the tile leaving.

followups: You may repaint at most m tiles. What is the longest all-black stretch you can make? (The window now has a variable size.)
Return the start index of a best window, the leftmost one on ties.
lcTitle: Minimum Recolors to Get K Consecutive Black Blocks
